title: Multi-Tenant Information Leakage via Database Schema Exposure
damaged_code:
```rust
#[derive(Serialize)]
struct TenantResource {
    tenant_db_schema_name: String, // Leaks internal database layout
    api_key: String,
}
```
pattern: Exposing physical database structural elements (such as schema names, raw partition keys, or table IDs) in public API response schemas.
why_bad: It presents a severe security risk and information leakage. It allows attackers to reconstruct internal network database topology, enabling SQL injections or multi-tenant partition bypasses.
detection: Match struct fields marked with `#[derive(Serialize)]` or exposed in public routes named `schema_name`, `table_name`, `partition_key`, or similar.
counterexample: Low-level internal diagnostic logs or administrative database control interfaces. Mark as `Context-dependent`.
fix:
Remove all internal storage database topology from public schemas. Use abstract tenant identifiers (like secure UUIDs) mapped internally on the server.
```rust
#[derive(Serialize)]
struct TenantResource {
    tenant_id: Uuid, // Abstract identifier
}
```
source: *Building Secure and Reliable Systems* by Heather Adkins et al. (Chapter 11, p. 238); *Implementing Domain-Driven Design* (Chapter 13).
